questions.q: The correct order in aqueous medium of basic strength in case of methyl substituted amines is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In aqueous medium basic strength is dependent on electron density on nitrogen as well as solvation of cation formed after accepting $H^{+}$. In~protic solvent like water, the order of basic strength is

${Me}_{2}NH > {MeNH}_{2} > {Me}_{3}N > {NH}_{3}$.

This happens beacuse~in case of~${Me}_{2}NH$~there will be optimum (+I) and solvation while in~${MeNH}_{2}$~has more significant hydration than~${Me}_{3}N$.

questions.q: The final product $A$, formed in the following multistep reaction sequence is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Bromobenzene reacts with magnesium in dry ether (diethyl ether) to form phenylmagnesium bromide, often abbreviated as $PhMgBr$.

The resulting phenylmagnesium bromide reacts with carbon dioxide in the presence of an acidic medium to form benzoic acid.

Heating benzoic acid with ammonia can lead to a reaction known as the Schotten-Baumann type reaction, which is a method for the amidation of carboxylic acids. In this reaction, the carboxylic acid group of benzoic acid reacts with ammonia to form an amide, benzamide, under heating conditions.

When an amide is treated with bromine in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide, degradation of amide takes place leading to the formation of primary amine.

In this case, it is an hoffmann bromamide reaction, aniline is formed.

questions.q: A compound  \left(x\right)$ with molar mass $108g{mol}^{- 1}$ undergoes acetylation to give product with molar mass $192g{mol}^{- 1}$. The number of amino groups in the compound  \left(x\right)$ is ________.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The compounds like amines and alcohols undergo acetylation with acetyl chloride. During this reaction, one proton of amine or alcohol is replaced with one acetyl group(${CH}_{3}CO -$).

The molar mass of the acetyl group is $43g / mol$. The increase in molar mass due to one acetyl group is $43 - 1 = 42g / mol$.

The molar mass of reactant is $108g / mol$. The molar mass of product is $192g / mol$. The change in mass is $84 .$

Hence, the number of acetyl groups $= \dfrac{84}{42} = 2$
